parallel.requirements: The run recognized ESM .mjs modules, manual command-line parsing, no external npm dependencies, DeepDiff-like string results, and a required /output delivery directory, but later conflated that delivery path with /workspace/output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent retained implementation and delivery ownership while delegating CLI and DeepDiff behavior probing to one child. The child returned findings, but it was never assigned implementation, integration, or final artifact placement.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented python_repr.mjs, unified_diff.mjs, deepdiff_strings.mjs, argparse_compat.mjs, and test1.mjs under /workspace/output, then patched the entrypoint and serializer after local checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The modules were internally compatible for local tests, but all created files were under /workspace/output. The parent did not copy or recreate them under /output before finalizing.
parallel.verification: The parent and child both probed the Python executable, and the parent verified the Node entrypoint with help, error, quote, NBSP, negative-like, and multiline cases, but all Node verification invoked /workspace/output/test1.mjs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The submitted artifact directory was empty and official evaluation scored 0 of 70. The visible process gap is the wrong delivery directory; any remaining algorithmic gaps are secondary because the evaluator had no files to run.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, manual parser, no external dependency, DeepDiff string output, and /output placement requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery, with no delegation or subagent handoff.
serial.implementation: The serial parent implemented a more modular /output tree with CLI, diff, format, and deepdiff libraries plus /output/test1.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was assembled directly under /output, and the parent listed the files from /output before final closure.
serial.verification: The serial parent compared the Node entrypoint from /output against the Python executable across normal, parser, quoting, control-character, and multiline diff cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The artifact was present and scored 67 of 70, but solution_passed remained false, indicating residual behavioral mismatch on three official samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run identified the required Node ESM, manual parser, DeepDiff output parity, and /output deliverable requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run identified the same requirements from the same prompt and explicitly planned to write /output/test1.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the material difference is that parallel later executed the delivery path as /workspace/output while serial used /output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent spawned one child to probe executable behavior while keeping implementation and final delivery with the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent performed probing, implementation, verification, and delivery itself with no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a probe-only child whose returned findings helped behavior mapping, but no separate implementation or assembly owner; serial used one continuous owner for every stage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child returned a usable behavior report to the parent, while the path placement requirement remained in the parent context and was not enforced at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept observations, implementation choices, and output placement in one context and planned /output/test1.mjs before writing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence of a bad child interface contract; the important context difference is global completion on a visible path mismatch in the parallel parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel implementation added five files under /workspace/output/lib and /workspace/output/test1.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial implementation added eight files under /output/lib and /output/test1.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented similar parser and DeepDiff-string logic, but the serial implementation was placed in the evaluator-visible directory and the parallel one was not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed and returned probe findings before the parent implementation phase, and the parent continued probing and implementing afterward.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle in the serial control; local findings stayed with the only actor until final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The child lifecycle itself did not lose work. The later failure was in parent final acceptance and delivery, not in a missing child join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integration assembled a coherent local module tree, but all writes and reads were rooted at /workspace/output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integration assembled the module tree in /output and confirmed the resulting file list there.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concurrent write collision is proven. The key shared-state difference is final workspace location: parallel used the wrong output tree while serial used the captured one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification ran targeted Node checks against /workspace/output/test1.mjs, then accepted the task as complete despite not checking /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification ran comparable Node checks against /output/test1.mjs and listed /output files before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial checks exercised the deliverable path the evaluator captured; the parallel checks exercised a different path and missed the deliverable-placement failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not time out, but used more agent time and closed after a final readback from /workspace/output rather than a /output acceptance check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also completed without timeout, used less agent time, listed /output files, and then closed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The difference is not raw budget exhaustion; it is closure quality. Parallel spent enough time to implement and test but did not close the delivery loop.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official pass/fail relation is both_fail because the current completed status evaluation sets solution_passed to false for both modes. The concrete task-solving difference is still large: the parallel run built and tested code under /workspace/output, then closed as if /output was populated, and the official artifact validation found no files so it scored 0 of 70. The serial run wrote and verified the deliverable under /output, artifact validation found the files, and it scored 67 of 70 but still failed the strict all-samples pass criterion.
parallel_contributors: Parent created, patched, and tested /workspace/output rather than the required /output tree.
Final response presented the task as complete and listed /workspace/output paths, leaving the evaluator-visible artifact empty.
serial_contributors: Serial parent created the module tree directly under /output.
Serial parent verified node /output/test1.mjs and listed /output files before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation still missed three of seventy official cases, which appears to be residual DeepDiff or argparse emulation drift rather than a coordination pattern.
Parallel may also have had residual emulation gaps, but official execution could not reach them because the artifact directory was empty.
evaluator_effects: Both modes have solution_passed false even though serial artifact_ok is true and serial passed 67 of 70 samples; the official relation therefore remains both_fail.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation for the artifact and score gap, not an official pass/fail outcome difference

candidates.reason: The parallel parent owned and performed implementation; the failure was not absence of an implementer.
There were no separately implemented components needing an unassigned integration owner; the parent integrated its own module tree.
The parent explicitly owned assembly and file creation, although it assembled in the wrong directory.
The parent owned probing, implementation, test, and delivery; the problem was an unsupported closure decision, not an ownerless pipeline.
Executable probing did not block all productive work behind one mandatory serial gate that caused unfinished implementation.
The parent and child overlapped probing, and implementation completed locally; there is no deadline-constrained investigation phase consequence.
No indispensable path was starved by auxiliary work; implementation and verification both occurred before closure.
The run used only one child and did not exhaust its wall-clock budget; the adverse effect was wrong-path completion.
The child had a bounded probing assignment and returned findings; it was not an overbroad child implementation task.
The child was asked to probe behavior, not to deliver files, so the /output placement requirement was not missing from a child implementation brief.
No separately owned components were delegated without an interface contract; the child returned observations only.
The child report preserved concrete findings; no known finding disappeared through transfer and forced repeated work.
The child report was structured and was not too large to consume; the parent continued using the behavior findings.
No child handoff described a superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then followed.
The parent did not receive conflicting child reports or unadjudicated contracts; there was only one child report.

The parent made a whole-task completion decision while the prompt-required /output placement remained visibly unverified: commands and final links used /workspace/output even as the final response claimed /output.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required deliverable location was not populated by the parallel parent before closure, leaving the run with an empty submitted artifact and no executable test1.mjs for official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: A placeable candidate existed under /workspace/output, but the decisive fault was the unsupported acceptance of a wrong-path deliverable, not a late or interrupted promotion attempt.

candidates.reason: There was no replacement or retry episode lacking inherited findings or current-file state.

candidates.reason: The child was not stopped or cancelled before completion; it returned a final report.
The same wrong-path delivery chain is better captured as unsupported global completion because the parent affirmatively closed as complete despite visible /workspace/output paths.
No child or implementation change was merged after integrated verification; verification followed the local implementation path.
The child did not produce an implementation requiring retrieval or merge; the parent implemented the code itself.
There was no verifier child with a trapped finding below the parent; the only child returned its report.
No required child failure, abort, or cancellation occurred that demanded takeover.
The parent received the completed child findings and continued with behavior-specific probes and implementation; no available result was ignored.
The parent did not wait blindly for a timeout; it actively probed, wrote, tested, patched, and finalized.
No concurrent agents wrote competing files or designs; only the parent wrote implementation files.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source file.
No agent overwrote another agent's non-entry source module.
No required entrypoint or submitted artifact was overwritten by another live actor.
No cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work.
The shared workspace was not destabilized by multiple live implementation writers; the only implementation writer was the parent.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, process, or temporary file from one actor was consumed by another as authoritative input.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent accepted and presented whole-task completion even though the known required output directory was /output and its own writes, tests, and final links used /workspace/output.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent closed with a wrong-path deliverable, so the required /output tree was not populated for the submitted artifact and official evaluation had no executable entrypoint to score.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The visible parent acceptance decision makes this an unsupported completion episode; late placement is only the downstream symptom of accepting the wrong output path as complete.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Late Finalization and No Assembly Owner were considered for the wrong-output chain but suppressed because the parent explicitly owned assembly and then accepted a visibly wrong delivery path as complete.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no child join, timeout, retry, handoff, write collision, or contamination episode independently cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label is retained for the wrong-output completion chain, with a unique episode, consequence, correction boundary, and evidence set.
